title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention and timeouts
author: Ravi Menon
description:
Motivation: operator-observed tail latency spikes and occasional request starvation in continuous-batcher under mixed workload profiles (short chat vs long-generation). This PR applies a set of conservative scheduler and queueing changes to reduce starvation, bound queueing delays, and make fairness policies more predictable across competing priority lanes.

What changed: consolidated several tuning knobs into a single SchedulerConfig, tightened max-queue-delay enforcement, introduced adaptive per-lane dequeue quotas to reduce head-of-line blocking, and added a starvation backoff path that promotes long-waiting requests after soft-timeout. Also added a global watchdog for per-request soft timeouts that triggers graceful eviction and retry hints instead of hard drops.

Key behavioral changes (user-visible):
- Short-running requests now have bounded extra queue delay: we enforce max_queue_delay_ms (default 40ms) per dequeue cycle.
- Fairness updated: per-lane adaptive quotas favor under-served lanes; long sequences are prevented from monopolizing batch slots.
- Starvation prevention: if a request waits longer than starvation_threshold_ms (default 250ms) it is elevated with a promotable token; promotion path schedules it into the next batch window.
- Soft timeouts: requests that exceed soft_timeout_ms receive a structured retry_hint in response metadata and are gracefully evicted to avoid cascading timeouts.

Testing and validation: microbenchmarks across 4xA10 nodes with mixed short/long workload showed 35-48% reduction in 99th-percentile queue delay for short requests and 15-22% reduction in end-to-end 99th latency for mixed traces. End-to-end integration tests added for starvation and soft-timeout behavior. CI flakiness addressed by increasing test harness timeouts for queue scheduling tests.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2; default enabled on canary for 48h with additional metrics dashboards: queue_delay_ms_per_lane, promoted_requests, soft_timeout_evictions. Will roll to prod if no regressions in token cost or p99 latency.

References: Linear ENG-4321, internal incident SUP-1187, prior continuous-batcher PRs for earlier fairness tuning.

review_comments: Sofia Lee: Can you explain how promotion interacts with batching window alignment? I want to ensure we don't create extra small batches.

Ravi Menon: Promotion attaches a promotable token but still respects the current batch window; promoted requests are placed into the next open slot and will not force an immediate batch flush unless window is nearly full.

human_readable_summary: This merged PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to reduce queueing delays and prevent request starvation by introducing adaptive per-lane quotas, a promotion path for long-waiting requests, and soft-timeout handling that returns retry hints instead of hard failures. Benchmarks show meaningful p99 improvements for mixed workloads with no cost regressions observed on canary.
